content_voiceover: This table is the T-cell counterpart to the B-cell cytogenetics slide, and the theme is the same: most of these translocations juxtapose an oncogene to a T-cell receptor locus, driving overexpression. Notice the pattern in the products column. The T-cell receptor genes are the partners, T R B on chromosome 7, T R A and T R D on chromosome 14. So when you see a breakpoint at 7 q 34 or 14 q 11, think T-cell receptor. The top rows are all T-lymphoblastic lymphoma, and the high-yield associations are the oncogenes each partner activates. The t 7;7 or inversion 7 drives HOXA cluster overexpression. The t 1;14 or t 1;7 drives TAL1, the single most classic oncogene in T-cell A L L. The t 7;9 activates NOTCH1, the master regulator of T-cell fate. The t 8;14 drives MYC, and the t 5;14 drives T L X 3. The individual frequencies are low, roughly three to five percent at most, so don't over-memorize the exact percents. The two rows examiners actually reward are at the bottom. The t 8;13 gives an FGFR2, ZMYM2 fusion tied to a myeloproliferative neoplasm associated with T-lymphoblastic lymphoma. And the money answer, the t 2;5, produces the A L K, N P M 1 fusion of anaplastic large cell lymphoma, accounting for about eighty-four percent of A L K-positive cases.
keypoints: T-cell partners = TCR loci: TRB (7q34), TRA/TRD (14q11)
t(1;14)/t(1;7) → TAL1; t(7;9) → NOTCH1 — classic T-ALL/T-LBL oncogenes
t(2;5)(p23;q35) → ALK::NPM1 = ALCL (~84% of ALK+ cases)
t(8;13) → FGFR2::ZMYM2 = MPN associated with T-LBL
keypoint_voiceover: Key points to lock in. The T-cell partner is almost always a T-cell receptor locus, T R B at 7 q 34 or T R A and T R D at 14 q 11. The t 1;14 and t 1;7 drive TAL1, and the t 7;9 drives NOTCH1, the classic T-lymphoblastic oncogenes. The one they love most, the t 2;5, gives the A L K, N P M 1 fusion of anaplastic large cell lymphoma, about eighty-four percent of A L K-positive cases. The t 8;13 gives an FGFR2, ZMYM2 fusion linked to a myeloproliferative neoplasm with T-L B L. And remember MYC from t 8;14 and T L X 3 from t 5;14.
